question: What is the impact of story 015-resource-time-buffer (BufferMinutes on ResourceType + Resources lifecycle events) on the current codebase?
claim:
MODULE: Resources — touched; ResourceType entity, ResourceInstance entity, and 6 command handlers (Create/Update/Delete for both types and instances) are in scope.
MODULE: Shared.Abstractions — touched, crossed-boundary; new event contracts must be added under Events/Resources/ (constitution Art. IV), the only existing coupling mechanism between modules.
MODULE: Availability — referenced by the story's intent but does not exist in the codebase today (capability-map.json lists only ManagementGroups, Resources, Users); the consuming side of the new events has no module to land in yet. Story explicitly puts Availability's own handling out of scope.
ENTITY: ResourceType (Resources.Core.Domain.ResourceType) — has no BufferMinutes property today; would need a new field plus Create/Update signature changes.
ENTITY: ResourceInstance (Resources.Core.Domain.ResourceInstance) — structurally unaffected; its Create/Delete command handlers must gain event publication.
ENDPOINT: POST /resources/types (Create resource type) — request/command must carry BufferMinutes (AC-1) and handler must publish ResourceSchemaCreatedEvent after SaveChangesAsync (AC-3); today it has neither.
ENDPOINT: PUT /resources/types/{id} (Update resource type) — request/command must carry BufferMinutes (AC-1); no publish requirement in AC.
ENDPOINT: GET /resources/types and GET /resources/types/{id} — response DTOs must include BufferMinutes (AC-2); today they do not.
ENDPOINT: DELETE /resources/types/{id} (Delete resource type) — handler must publish ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent (AC-5); today it publishes nothing.
ENDPOINT: POST /resources/instances (Create resource instance) — handler must publish ResourceInstanceCreatedEvent (AC-4); today it publishes nothing.
ENDPOINT: DELETE /resources/instances/{id} (Delete resource instance) — handler must publish ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent (AC-6); today it publishes nothing.
SCREEN: frontend/src/app/features/schemas/schemas.routes.ts (routes "new", ":schemaId") — existing screens consume resource-schema data, but the story explicitly marks frontend changes out of scope, so no screen change is required by this story.
EVENT: none exist yet — Shared.Abstractions/Events/ only has ManagementGroups/ and Users/ subfolders, no Resources/ subfolder; new contracts needed: ResourceSchemaCreatedEvent, ResourceInstanceCreatedEvent, ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent, ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent.
SCHEMA: likely change — ResourceType has no BufferMinutes column in its current EF configuration/entity; a new EF migration in Resources.Migrations is required per constitution Art. VI.
BLOCKED_BY: Availability module does not exist in the codebase (capability-map.json modules = ManagementGroups, Resources, Users only) — acceptable per the story's own out-of-scope note (consumer side is a separate story), but flagged as a fact since the new events will have zero subscribers until Availability is built.
BLOCKED_BY: the BufferMinutes upper validation limit is not defined anywhere in the codebase or the story text (AC-1 only says "reasonable upper limit"); epic open decision no. 3 (source of truth for the buffer: Resources vs Availability) is explicitly still open per the story frontmatter.
RISK: DeleteResourceTypeCommandHandler soft-deletes a schema's instances via a bulk ExecuteUpdateAsync (SoftDeleteInstancesAsync), not through ResourceInstance.Delete() — so instances belonging to a deleted schema will not individually raise ResourceInstanceDeletedEvent; only ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent fires for the schema itself.
RISK: GroupDeletedHandler hard-deletes all ResourceTypes for a group via a bulk ExecuteDeleteAsync — confirmed no per-schema ResourceSchemaDeletedEvent will be published on group deletion; this matches the story's stated out-of-scope design (Availability must react to GroupDeleted separately) but is a real behavioural gap if not handled.
RISK: no new authorization gap identified — CreateResourceTypeCommandHandler already enforces group.OwnerId == command.CallerId for schema creation; adding BufferMinutes to existing create/update paths does not introduce a new authz surface (consistent with story's touches_authz: false).
